pl256197.description: An ancient sanctuary of Hercules (Melqart) that Strabo places at one end of the long island (Cotinussa) that extended south from ancient Gades. Significant landscape and coastal change have occurred since antiquity, disrupting the integrity of these islands. Nonetheless, modern scholars have consistently identified the location of the sanctuary as at or near the 17th-18th century Castillio de Sancti Petri, which today occupies a separate homonymous islet. pl113543066.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl113543066.description: A Spanish village located to the west of Sevilla, Spain. In the thirteenth century, it belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. The site was known as Sanlúcar de Albaida until it took the definitive name of Albaida de Aljarafe.

cur-fossil-jebel-irhoud.dateNote: Barite miners found a human skull here in Morocco in 1961. New digs and dates in 2017 put the bones at about 315,000 years old (0.3 million years) — the oldest Homo sapiens known.

pl390312807.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl390312807.description: Gabia La Grande (Granada, Spain) is the findspot of a subterranean nymphaeum approached by a dromos that may have dated to the fourth century CE.

cur-fossil-ouled-abdoun.dateNote: The phosphate mines of this basin near Khouribga, Morocco, are full of sharks, sea reptiles and early mammals. In 2009 Emmanuel Gheerbrant named Eritherium from here, one of the oldest relatives of elephants. About 60 million years old (Paleocene).
cur-fossil-ouled-abdoun.summary: Moroccan phosphate mines that gave up Eritherium, one of the first elephant relatives.

cur-fossil-fezouata.dateNote: Mohamed Ben Moula, a local fossil collector, found soft-bodied fossils in these shales north of Zagora, Morocco. In 2010 Peter Van Roy's team reported them: animals like those of the Burgess Shale, but younger. The rock is about 480 million years old (Early Ordovician). Wikidata pins the formation at a rounded point.
cur-fossil-fezouata.summary: Moroccan shales that keep soft-bodied sea animals from about 480 million years ago.

cur-find-taforalt.dateNote: DNA from burials in this Moroccan cave, about 15,000 years old, showed the people had ancestry from both the Near East and sub-Saharan Africa (van de Loosdrecht et al., Science, 2018).

cur-fossil-kem-kem.dateNote: In 2018 Nizar Ibrahim's team dug the tail of a Spinosaurus out of the Kem Kem beds of south-east Morocco. Its paddle-like tail showed this giant hunted in water. The rock is about 100–95 million years old (Late Cretaceous). Wikidata pins the beds at a rounded point.
cur-fossil-kem-kem.summary: Where a Spinosaurus tail showed the giant swam, in the Moroccan desert.

cur-find-bizmoune.dateNote: Thirty-three pierced sea-snail shells from a cave near Essaouira, Morocco, at least 142,000 years old: the oldest shell beads yet found (Sehasseh et al., Science Advances, 2021).
